groups.title: OpenWave empirical criteria
groups.purpose: Assess the 31 OpenWave physical targets locally on every registered RER law. The public M10 column at the cited revision pins Interval Echo. OpenWave partially validated Row 4 and marked the other 30 rows as not yet tested. Each RER grade describes the measurement and scope named in its entry.

criteria.title: Charge quantization
criteria.requires: Exhibit an integer topological electric charge and exclude division of one unit between two half-charged excitations.

interval_echo.note: Two compact vacancy modes share a single missing load over cells 5, 11 and 23 owner steps apart on three boards. Paired contact reads distinguish that state from independent preparations with the same local means on each board in a fresh precision replicate. At every free appointment the reduced state of the gateways and blank collars on either tested enclosing cut equals the filled host, even on a branch with the vacancy wholly inside. A single load and a doubled load also persist on empty hosts. The measurements select neither a topological electric unit nor an electric charge law excluding two half-charge daughters.

comparison.finding: In 18 half-transfer fixtures the sharp regional head flux follows the whole signed load. A head-independent control has 50% mismatch. The integer step is supplied by the alphabets.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: Integer port loads and their conserved populations are measured in the coherent blank sector. Establishing an electric topological charge and excluding physical half-charge daughters requires a charge readout.

scalar_channel.note: Electric topological charge and a forbidden splitting channel have yet to be identified.

criteria.title: Electron rest energy (mass)
criteria.requires: Select a localized state dynamically. With its energy anchored at 511 keV, predict and independently measure another physical quantity fixed by that anchor.

interval_echo.note: Gateway monitoring holds a compact vacancy. With a material clock and six-seam storage, separate joint reads give 35 for one vacancy and 70 for two separated copies. A changed pair interaction shifts the two-copy reading. A vacancy and excess give 35 and 67 with this reference, or 43 each with five-seam storage. Independent storage readings account for the difference. A local phase flip lowers the mean vacancy energy. A local pulse releases charge from that same held vacancy. On 20, 80 and 320 cells the native one-vacancy spectrum excludes the relativistic recoil energy at pc = 511 keV with the six-seam anchor. Its identification with an electron rest threshold remains open. Preparing two vacancies and an excess gives a repulsively bound charged trimer. The upper-band configuration stays intact with probability at least 0.5745 at all exposures on the 20-cell board and 0.7298 on both refinements. Its host-referenced recoil target exceeds the whole sector ceiling on every board. Internal rearrangement is observed and translational inertia remains unresolved.

comparison.finding: The mobile four-face input has mean energy 17 and standard deviation 8 in native units. Its charged gate has a nondegenerate floor of 3.5480114451 with the external compensator held fixed. Other preparations have different formation edges. The 510.999 keV reconstruction uses laboratory inputs alone.

demonstrated_measurement.label: Two separated vacancies give twice the anchored energy

additional_comparisons.label: Recoil of a locally prepared charge eleven links away
additional_comparisons.finding: From one untagged vacancy the ideal interferometer resolves three lines. The one-anchor heavy energy agrees within the tau uncertainty. The middle ratio is high by 9.83 ppm across an exact scale audit and simulated acquisitions. A finite clock changes the ratios, with cadence fitted from the muon. These are within-charge frequency differences. A scalar impulse on the same parked mode gives zero recoil while a mobile vacancy responds. On the moving unpinned guide two positive recoil gaps per branch recover the same ratios without a charged-sector energy zero and predict a third spatial mode. After a signed local source click, the same vacancy travels eleven links. Distal counts recover three dispersion masses and spatial reads identify their wavelengths. Shutters hold the source, and the register mass term is supplied.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: The free contrast interaction binds localized loads and has measurable binding energies. Electron identification, rest-energy calibration and an independent physical prediction from 511 keV remain open.

scalar_channel.note: A prepared four-seam branch has a measured single-addition gap. Two separated additions give the sum in joint phase records. The 511 keV anchor alone supplies a scale. An independent electron observable and identification remain open.

criteria.title: de Broglie clock (Zitterbewegung)
criteria.requires: Measure an internally initiated, frequency-rigid oscillation whose angular frequency equals the measured rest energy divided by ℏ.

interval_echo.note: A sharp vacancy with monitored gateways gives a free internal beat at 2.237 and 2.232 per independently timed exchange unit on 80 and 320 cells. Halving the contrast shifts its mean energy relative to the uniform host from 34.62 to 18.62 while leaving the beat at 2.234. The full blank one-vacancy spectrum is contained in [32,54] on all three boards, so an internal frequency equal to the separately measured 35-unit vacancy transfer is excluded in this sector. Even without monitoring, a sharp vacancy on each larger board contributes a cosine at √5 with coefficient at least 1/40 in its free return probability. The material timer and terminal reads are supplied apparatus.

comparison.finding: In the repaired periodic medium a central-port oscillation has native angular frequency 16.49242250. Every nonzero translation-invariant one-end beat is at least 4, above the one-end formation edge 1.753788749.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: A spontaneously starting oscillation tied to an independently measured rest energy remains open.

scalar_channel.note: After a finite preparation pulse two local clocks resolve a free line at about 4.89898, agreeing with a separate fuel-gap measurement. Autonomous onset and the electron rest-energy identification remain open.

criteria.title: Particle stability (Derrick escape)
criteria.requires: Release the prepared particle state and measure its persistence under free evolution. Identify the excitation and the domain of the measurement. The separate SM-e entry assesses its identification as an electron.

private_record_walk.note: The unweighted private graph predicts pair persistence on its declared spectator preparation. A single-load survey and the equal-load comparison law give the full contact response. The sharp launch-sign and material readout tests the microscopic source separately. This experimental candidate has no OpenWave pin decision.

demonstrated_measurement.label: Free persistence of a prepared pair

interval_echo.note: Free persistence is demonstrated locally for a prepared pair of unassigned species. At held exposure 37 the launch patch has adjacent-pair probability 0.98027 at κ = 8 versus 0.20291 at κ = 0. Seeded records gave 4,028 versus 824 detections in 4,096 draws per arm. For that cell-13 launch the home probability stays at least 0.94 through exposure 37. OpenWave reproduced the probabilities and partially validated the historical pin, whose design search compared strengths using persistence. A later law uses the same signed-record comparison for exchange parity and eight incident witnesses on a shielded standard cell. Its magnitude-one energy is exactly 8, reproducing the binary-pair generator. With a one-port preparation calibrated by stationarity, its magnitude-two energy is exactly 32 and the complete seam generator agrees. A direct simulation recorded 104 transitions from lower modes into magnitude two. The 17-offer digital realization also passes the phase-gate tolerance and all 24 material reunion comparisons. The target was known when the comparator and uniform deployment were chosen. Using fair parity instead approaches 4. The portable contact instrument distinguishes κ = 8 from all eight other published strengths and a pair-only rival before release. For adjacent launches on the stated federation class the probability of adjacency anywhere is at least 5/6 at every exposure. The cell-13 home-pair probability is at least 0.96325 through exposure 37. On the 20-cell board, all 600 internal launch seams clear both sampling forecasts. At exposure 37, 24 have home probability below 0.94. At κ = 8 the 630 distinct-load band levels lie below the two-free-load rest reference. At κ = −8 they lie above the free exchange band. A separate source equates an empty primitive collar bank’s differential frequency to the material coefficient and obtains κ = 8. The zero-strength donor gives the same calibration fringe. This equality was chosen with the persistence results known. The historical pair's coupling has no independent selection in the published sweep. The archived clock and vacuum fringes agree at κ = ½ and 8 while the original home-pair probabilities at exposure 37 differ by more than 0.56. A distinct single-load source passes the free home-cell test for every real coupling on all 420 cells, including preparation exhaustion. Its all-time joint home probability is at least 0.999940596800. OpenWave awarded Partial to the historical pair. The single-load registration is prepared for owner review. Its changed state and detector require adjudication and its task-selected confirmation is pending. Full-credit filing is on HOLD.

comparison.finding: An oriented neutral dipole persists at every reading across all 630 intercell seams. Changing one neighbouring head permits separation. The prepared field orientation blocks the original moves.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: The registered seam emitter prepares a pair that retains adjacency during free flight. The finite records resolve the pair and the binding theorem bounds loss of adjacency for all times on the spherical federation.

scalar_channel.note: With the registered cage preparation and terminal reader on one cell, the four-seam excitation persists at five free waits. Its invariant subspace keeps it localized for all times under the scalar channel's free generator.

criteria.title: Magnetic moment μ (g ≈ 2, magnetostatics)
criteria.requires: Measure a static magnetic dipole sourced by internal circulation in the stationary electron, its gyromagnetic factor near two and its Larmor response.

interval_echo.note: Each owner on the 20-, 80- and 320-cell federations supports a compact stationary vacancy with signed material current. The measured precession frequency of a tilted current vector is 0.011053 per exchange unit, with 99% interval [0.010940,0.011161], against 0.011049 from the zero-field moments and applied flux. A probe constrained outside the source cell has exactly the same channel for either current and for no source. This strictly compact degenerate band has zero recoil under the owner momentum kick. An orthogonal, dispersive orbital carries the vacancy and its direction to another owner, with one-hop signed moment +0.001409 versus −0.000485 per launch. Its broad energy distribution separates this mobile preparation from the precisely stationary compact band. A static exterior dipole field and independent finite inertial mass and spin standards for an electron gyromagnetic factor are unresolved. On a ten-port orbital belt, flux splitting and independent small-momentum recoil gave g_orb = 0.63327 [0.61951, 0.64710] at simultaneous 99% coverage. Using the first finite recoil gap instead gave 0.70804 and missed the held second gap. These ratios exclude g near two for that orbital.

comparison.finding: An imposed half-quantum twist changes a charge-return probability from 14.7898% to 93.3966%. The unique real resting ground has zero signed current and zero first-order magnetic slope. The measured response is orbital.

demonstrated_measurement.label: Stationary vacancy current and its precession in an applied flux

additional_comparisons.law: Two material rings coupled by native contacts on a controlled schedule
additional_comparisons.finding: The source circulation rotates a probe on the adjacent ring. With weak, periodic contact an independent return-phase calibration predicts 40 held rotations within 0.017 radians. Reversing the source direction reverses the rotation. Reversing only the material probe charge preserves its sign at both contact durations. With continuous protection of the source momentum, the generators seen by the probe agree for opposite directions.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: The electron dipole, gyromagnetic factor and field-driven precession require an electromagnetic readout.

scalar_channel.note: The electron dipole, gyromagnetic factor and field-driven precession require an electromagnetic readout.

criteria.title: Angular momentum J (spin ℏ/2)
criteria.requires: Measure angular momentum of magnitude ℏ/2 carried by the field of the same electron state.

interval_echo.note: A signed defect transmits two coherent orbital modes across two cell boundaries on each native host. These modes are spatial orientations. Field angular momentum of magnitude ℏ/2 on an identified electron remains unmeasured.

comparison.finding: The four-face state transports a coherent pair of orbital modes. A 2% single-ring rate perturbation splits the parked degeneracy. A spinorial physical rotation and intrinsic angular momentum of this mobile state are unresolved.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: Field angular momentum has yet to be measured on an identified electron.

scalar_channel.note: Field angular momentum has yet to be measured on an identified electron.

criteria.title: Spin-½ statistics (720° double cover)
criteria.requires: Interfere a full rotation, or a two-core exchange, with a reference and recover a minus sign. A dynamically selected half-turn discriminated from a polar control provides intermediate evidence.

interval_echo.note: On the freely arriving signed orbital, a controlled full template turn and opposite orders of perpendicular half-turns give positive relative phase. Two addressed orbital packets exchange with +SWAP. The same apparatus resolves the imposed spinorial and odd-permutation signs. This orbital construction fails the requested double-cover test.

comparison.finding: A fermionic spin singlet reproduces the two-charge counts. The matched three-input load gives 37.33% arrival where any spin-½ fermion input with the same spin-independent transfers gives zero. In a separate four-face preparation a fixed material exchange restores all 16 head inputs and leaves the different orbital states at their original cells.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: A physical rotation or exchange phase and its polar control remain unmeasured.

scalar_channel.note: The scalar register construction uses fermionic operators. An interference measurement of a dynamically selected two-core exchange or 2π rotation remains open.

criteria.title: Antimatter + annihilation
criteria.requires: Observe a particle and its conjugate convert into radiation. Resolve the two- and three-photon positronium channels as follow-up measurements.

interval_echo.note: Observers prepare opposite phase walls on a closed four-dimer ring. During free registered evolution with fixed number guards the walls can disappear. On three-dimer wings 8,245,757 of 268,435,456 launches gave an ordered ring and excitation on both sides, against 914 on the ordered sham. After the source measurement the local energy rose at two radii on each side. The regional current has zero matrix elements within the wall-free wing subspace. These records identify annihilation of opposite order defects and energy transfer in neutral material. An electric particle–antiparticle assignment and outgoing radiation quanta remain open. A separate registered coincidence service erases an excess and a vacancy, whose free numbers are individually conserved. Before a source measurement the 65-unit wall surplus left 62.9782 units inside the ring and 1.1321 in the two guide interiors at exposure 32. On initially uniform unguarded receivers, restoring the ring consumes all four vacancies and doubles and excludes positive receiver energy. Remote material counts verify both receivers are active. The sourced outgoing energy on the disappearing-pair trials remains unresolved. OpenWave’s accepted liquid-crystal example leaves the outgoing radiation type open.

comparison.finding: The free written law preserves excess and vacancy counts separately. An external pair-conversion contact sends a neutral disturbance to a probe six cell steps away. Spontaneous conversion and photon multiplicities have no measurement in this run.

demonstrated_measurement.label: Opposite phase walls disappear and energy reaches two radii on both sides

additional_comparisons.law: Time-independent local conversion term added to the native encounter Hamiltonian
additional_comparisons.finding: The added term converts an initially separated pair without a trigger and conserves the total energy of the held system. After 64 exchange units, outer-dimer frequency-selective readings gave 1,017 hard/soft double clicks in 1,073,741,824 launches at the stated detector settings. Two wings above 16 energy units gave zero double clicks in that bank. The energy carriers are excitations of the prepared neutral medium.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: The free contrast term preserves load. An identified conjugate pair converting into outgoing field quanta has yet to be measured.

scalar_channel.note: Local instruments distinguish adding and removing an object from the filled reference. The sharp cage occupations persist during free evolution. A radiative annihilation channel requires different evidence.

criteria.title: Neutrinos (neutral states)
criteria.requires: Identify electrically neutral, light excitations among the products of a decay.

interval_echo.note: Production in a decay, electric neutrality and lightness have yet to be established for the same excitation.

comparison.finding: Six downward charged-mode channels produce positive neutral field energy after a bridge switch. The separated daughter and neutral spectra miss the isolated parent energy in every channel. The experiment supplies neither neutrino flavour tags nor a neutrino mass.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: Production in a decay, electric neutrality and lightness have yet to be established for the same excitation.

scalar_channel.note: The scalar law supports neutral excitations relative to its supplied gauge reference. A light neutral product released in a weak decay remains unidentified.

criteria.title: Neutrino oscillations (PMNS)
criteria.requires: Distinguish three neutrino flavours through production and detection, observe their oscillations and extract the PMNS angles.

interval_echo.note: A flavour-tagged source, transitions and a mixing-angle determination remain open.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: A flavour-tagged source, transitions and a mixing-angle determination remain open.

scalar_channel.note: The resolved bands belong to one scalar channel. Three flavour-labelled channels, their oscillations and mixing angles remain open.

criteria.title: Lepton mass spectrum (μ, τ)
criteria.requires: Resolve precisely three charged-lepton minima and compare their relative masses with 1, 207 and 3477.

interval_echo.note: For all net negative-unit compositions of the registered blank-memory law, the maximum ratio between host-referenced composition ground energies is bounded above by 57.5625, 203.296875 and 759.546875 on the 20-, 80- and 320-cell boards. This excludes 3477 in those spectra. In the same architecture on any finite refinement a 3477 ratio of these minima needs at least 2319 defect ports in the heavier configuration. On a ten-port belt three dressings selected for closeness have first-wavelength recoil inertia ratios 1:168.56:3209.78 and second-wavelength ratios 1:164.91:3301.44. Their formation energies are in the ratios 1:2.01:2.81. Signed density records verify motion. Identifying three charged species with consistent recoil and formation energies requires another preparation.

comparison.finding: Three independently prepared orbital bands have minimum-energy ratios 1 : 4.56155 : 10.40388 on the 48-cell route. Exact inequalities exclude the balanced Koide value for every triplet from the two fully written one-cell sectors. A separate first-order extension with a supplied register mass operator gives 1 : 206.770316 : 3477.472837 on a seven-cell corridor of degree-six ports. One added degree-five port collapses the hierarchy. The physical species, unconfined mass poles and clock calibration are unresolved.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: No three minima have been identified as charged leptons and compared on a common mass scale.

scalar_channel.note: Several scalar lines have measured frequencies for a supplied level parameter. A charged-lepton family assignment and three mass ratios remain open.

criteria.title: Quarks
criteria.requires: Recover fractional electric charge from a partial winding of a quark string.

interval_echo.note: Two polar probes covering the ten-port belt measure its integral total on moving period-three walls and same-load compact preparations. Subtracting the separately measured one-in-three bulk density gives identical fractional excesses on these controls. A stationary probe in an adjacent cell records a phase when material can enter the intervening gateway. With the registered open-boundary reference, changing the probe sign or using a matched compact preparation changes that phase outside a common fractional-charge calibration. Electric charge on the winding defect requires a field with an independent electric standard. A separate prepared written-head string has a fractional static signed-field response calibrated against an ordinary unit. Free relaxation of that polarization and the unresolved physical electric standard limit the identification. On a prepared ternary string, a differential signed contact probe recovers the same fractional material response after adding zero through four neutral pairs. All 7,590 ternary words at total 13 or 14 on the ten-port guide have simple spectrum within each translation momentum, including across histograms. On parked three-wall preparations a remote six-dimer material guide gives −0.3307 and +0.6656 ordinary units seven or eight native seams from an end belt. This is a segmented material-polarization measurement. The unit-calibrated unsplit electrode gives almost zero for two simultaneous units. The exact local port and memory symmetry algebra of the free seam and the echo is abelian. The complete uniform written-head cut gives zero imaginary response at a half turn on any state, while the two smooth wall apertures resolve opposite signed responses. A time-ordered circuit of native contacts sustains period-three material order on a twelve-port cell. Translating an equal-count compact control also gives the third-turn polarization shift. A common external material reference on the released 15-port ring and reservoir gives signed +⅔ and −⅓ readings on the same stationary states as the triple detections. A diagonal change of head phase removes every flat material twist of the unit-memory graph. The charge interpretation still depends on the smoothed periodic reference.

comparison.finding: On two antipodal field-endpoint preparations a material tour resolves winding while both regional signed-charge meters read zero. An imposed third-turn phase is recovered from the receiver ports with zero excess flux on every cut of the 458-word field component. Calibrated whole loads coherently shared over three ports give fractional means and integer outcomes.

additional_comparisons.law: Period-three material walls on native contacts
additional_comparisons.finding: On prepared ten-port belts a one-site slip in period-three order carries material excess −⅓ or +⅔ in two static cuts and the same signed current ratio at launch. On an intact cell, the probability of detecting each wall type exceeds 97% at exposure 16 when all six axes are accepted. A uniform regional voltage has integral sharp outcomes. The aligned written heads register −1 or +2 transported units per three wall circuits. The physical electric coupling is unresolved.

additional_comparisons.law: Registered material exchanges with an externally threaded transport phase
additional_comparisons.finding: The sharp three- and four-load walls respond exactly as material charges −⅓ and +⅔ upon translation. Against 12 held opposite-twist splittings per freely dressed wall the rigid predictions miss by 0.01596 and 0.01373, above the declared 0.01 tolerance. Integer competitors miss by at least 0.37831 and 0.33070. Including all virtual excursions predicts 24 additional readings within 0.00035 exchange units. A full flux cycle gives the same momentum shift for a nonwinding control with equal total load. The flux and coherent reference are supplied.

A signed test load measures −0.33360 or +0.66640 ordinary units at a partial density winding on a prepared 313-port guide. Both probe signs resolve the classes in a held aperture. The smooth-cut read cancels around both ends. Free release changes the polarization at quadratic order. A universal electric coupling and quark identity are unestablished.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: An electric response tied to fractional string winding remains unmeasured.

scalar_channel.note: An electric response tied to fractional string winding remains unmeasured.

criteria.title: Baryons: bound state (p, n)
criteria.requires: Recover a persistent bound composite whose three constituents are identified as quarks.

interval_echo.note: Three ordinary loads bind on a triangular face in the free contrast interaction. The constituent charge, colour and baryon identity remain open. On three connected ten-port guides, the registered low-energy subspace below the mean energy of three separated clusters has at most 0.181% or 0.149% probability of containing all three fractionally polarized wall records, for net material excess zero or one. This bound allows every configuration with the same ordinary load count. An upper-band composite or a different dressed-wall read requires separate evidence. With the exterior shuttered a sharp triangular face and finite energy filter at 100.448 give a persistent singlet component in three locally decoded colour triplets. At 32 free exchange units, 32,525 of 72,008 accepted face-and-three-triplet reads are antisymmetric singlet (524,288 total launches), above the one-third biseparable bound. A separate common half-turn gives a resolved dark-port signal on three-triplet records. The material loads are integral, and the fitted colour readers are supplied. The joined uppermost state gives simultaneous fractional wall records with probability at least 73.59% (neutral) or 70.55% (positive). Its energy exceeds the upper edge with a bridge deleted. Retaining the local cost of a hop into an empty site at each cut end puts a separated pair-plus-single trial above the entire joined spectrum in both cases. On the fully opened 80-cell board any stationary state confined to the three complete source owners has at most 21.10% or 24.70% joint wall probability in the neutral or positive sector. A separate threefold compact orbital on 128 owners supports an exact antisymmetric orbital singlet with zero energy gained relative to its separated fragments. With arbitrary tails and all wall charts and positions admitted, the lower-energy band below separated cluster trials yields at most 0.274% neutral or 0.226% positive three-wall reads on all three boards. In the separate three-ordinary-load sector, an open-board trimer band has at least 95.01% face probability and lies at least 26.5 native units below separated pair-plus-single configurations. Its positive ground state gives zero geometric phase under adiabatic scalar rotations. A separate fifteen-site mobile string coupled to a held commensurate reference gives at most 31.81% or 50.68% for three charged gap records in their shortest arc. Requiring three separate sets of material sites leaves only the widest arc, with at most 19.12% or 22.78% probability. On a complete 20-cell board with an outward prepared field the held 15-port extension yields 85.25% neutral and 20.27% positive tight triples on separate stationary lines. Opening a neighbouring reservoir gives 80.90% and 9.45% in the designated channels of one Hamiltonian. All 885,726 mobile-background sharp triples at lengths 12, 15 and 18 have jointly injective transfer to the complement within each sector. Binding against every fragmentation channel and physical constituent identifications remain open.

comparison.law: Interval Echo with three guarded one-load colour readers
comparison.finding: At one free exchange time the three loads occupy a face with probability 0.98115. Each detected tip reads +1 material unit against empty. Every accepted face-supported state has collective-centre dark probability at least 63/256 in the ideal instrument across all 5,775 balanced routings. With a common port frame, reflection symmetry gives exactly zero three-triplet singlet overlap for the full 220-configuration ground state. The electromagnetic unit and quark flavours remain unassigned.

additional_comparisons.law: Period-three material walls on native contacts
additional_comparisons.finding: Across all 3,000 sharp placements per integer total, native exchanges force both three-wall spaces to leak. On an eighteen-site shared comparison string stationary three-gap probability reaches 94.19% or 97.80%, while the tightest triple reaches 43.65% or 14.88%. A rotation-independent colour triplet is excluded in the measured one-cell wall bands. A bound proton or neutron is unidentified.

additional_comparisons.law: Three walls with active written contacts
additional_comparisons.finding: On 18 native ports, optimization over every stationary state yields at most 15.58% tight three-wall weight for the neutral source and 9.77% or 14.72% for two positive sectors. In the tested intact-cell components four-hop material records distinguish all joint matter and field configurations, excluding an exact internal colour triplet commuting with the full material read. Three degree-preserving rotations produce equal spectra on distinct Gauss backgrounds for each wall. Material hops, field flips and occupation measurements preserve each background and give identical probabilities on a three-copy determinant and its permutation mixture.

contrast_memory_spherical_v1.note: Three ordinary loads bind on a triangular face in the free contrast interaction. The constituent charge, colour and baryon identity remain open.

scalar_channel.note: A three-quark identification remains open.

The gateway-centred neutral material profile has a positive outermost shell. Both the reference contribution and the choice of centre enter this measurement.

criteria.title: Dark matter candidate
criteria.requires: Demonstrate a stable massive excitation with measured neutrality as a dark-matter candidate.

interval_echo.note: In a supplied uniformly filled medium a freely released excess and vacancy have zero relative load charge. A separated upper spectral band has an all-exposure lower bound of 85.47% for binding at the selected degree type on 20, 80 and 320 cells. At exposure 32 on 20 cells, 99.44% of terminal outcomes were adjacent, and in 6.83% both constituents had changed sites and were adjacent. Most motion stayed within the launch cell. An electromagnetic charge measurement and an independent inertial mass for this same excitation remain open. This test addresses OpenWave’s particle criterion. The OPH dark-sector paper assigns gravitational stress to anomalous modular charge on an overlap collar. Pair binding provides no measurement of that source. OpenWave lists OPH as untested on Row 19 at the cited revision. The official static test asks for a stable neutral massive state. It does not specify an elementary particle or a relic abundance. PATCH-10 tracks gravitational observations sourced by patch records. A separate coin-odd contrast-two memory has fixed-address native gaps of 32 or 33. Every one of the nine two-port load inputs acquires the same energy shift. Excess and vacancy Ramsey probes return bright with probability one at π/32, against zero for the matched even-coin contact. This identifies a stored mode invisible to these probes. Electromagnetic neutrality and a finite inertial mass require independent evidence. Matched collar correlations on a separate 20-cell native four-tracer instrument produce zero exact initial focusing contrast. At the later appointment their normalized chord volumes differ by −0.000005833 ± 0.000001756 at simultaneous 99% coverage. Testing anomalous gravitational stress requires a common proper curvature coupled to the collar, beyond this tracer geometry. This broader hypothesis is separate from the static particle criterion. Three free bound-pair preparations on a 20-cell uniformly filled host give measured intercell kinetic matrix elements near −1.02 to −1.04 × 10⁻⁶ exchange units. Their intact-pair terminal imbalance responds to the imposed phase. The branch polarizes under a spatially stepped signed-load impulse while its total relative load stays zero. Inertial mass from momentum dispersion and coupling to a physical electromagnetic field remain unmeasured.
